bootstrap.method: events resampled for recall, precision, F1 and category accuracy (true segments stay with their event); whole days resampled for false alarms; same draws for every model on a set; percentile intervals

verdict_rule.metric: event-counted F1 (the objective tuned on validation): recall = detected events / events, precision = detected events / (detected events + false alarms), each detected event counted once
verdict_rule.comparison: paired bootstrap of F1(selected fusion design) minus F1(threshold voting): the same resampled events and days are applied to both models (1000 resamples, seed 12345)
verdict_rule.beats: the 95% interval of the difference lies entirely above 0 AND the fusion design's false alarms/day on that test set are within the cap
verdict_rule.worse: the 95% interval of the difference lies entirely below 0
verdict_rule.also_reported: the same paired difference for segment-based F1, false alarms/day and category accuracy, and the cap status of both models; these do not change the verdict

notes.test_v3: HEADLINE. Fresh scenario test events (seed 20261011), generated after the test_v2 incident. Frozen first, then every model evaluated exactly once. Its file was loaded and featurised once by a dry run before the freeze; no model or metric used its test rows before the final run.
notes.test_v2: SECONDARY. Fresh scenario test events (seed 20261010). The baselines (fixed_threshold, isolation_forest, ocsvm) were scored on this set once before the freeze by mistake, so their rows here are a second access; all other models are evaluated on it here for the first time.
notes.test_v1_exposed: Round-1 scenario test events; exposed for F-B. Reference only.
notes.battledim_test_previously_exposed: BattLeDIM test split (8 events); exposed for F-B in Round 1, cannot be refreshed. Infrastructure evidence only. Decision parameters were tuned on the BattLeDIM validation split with the same procedure and cap.
